The official event page names percussionists Selvaganesh Vinayakram and Amit Kavthekar alongside Shankar and describes a program of ragas, extended improvisation and intricate rhythmic interplay centered on Shankar's stereophonic double violin and voice. en.why_it_matters: This is not admission by the Shakti name alone. Shankar's wide-register double violin and voice meet two percussionists whose rhythmic vocabularies can turn a raga into an elastic three-way conversation. The exact trio gives the living East-West fusion lineage a present-tense instrumental form rather than treating it as repertory history.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for the local February 27 date if violin, Indian rhythm or fusion sits on the listening thread. It is a strong A+ trio in an intimate room, not evidence for changing a larger trip or treating the night as a farewell.

events.category: Cross-cultural string duet / Kora translation / Raga improvisation
events.factual_description: Wolf Trap and District of Raga present Derek Gripper and Alam Khan at The Barns on Friday, March 5, 2027 at 8:00 PM, with doors at 6:30 PM. The primary event page describes Gripper mapping the technique and artistry of the 21-string African kora onto classical guitar and Khan, son of Ali Akbar Khan, bringing sarod and raga improvisation. The announced duet is framed as spontaneous collaboration across African and Indian plucked-string traditions. Wolf Trap's presale notice places the performance in the new November 10 tranche, with public sales scheduled for November 13 at 10:00 AM ET.

en.why_it_matters: Gripper's guitar already makes the interlocking motion of kora music audible on six strings; Alam Khan adds a sarod language built around raga development and inherited from Ali Akbar Khan. The value is the live duet itself: two systems of resonance and improvisation negotiating melody in real time, not a generic world-music pairing.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for this local Friday if plucked strings, raga or musical translation matters. The pairing lifts the date above Gripper's nearby solo program, while no premiere or last-chance claim supports a scarcity tier.

es.why_it_matters: La guitarra de Gripper ya vuelve audible en seis cuerdas el movimiento entrelazado de la kora; Alam Khan suma un lenguaje de sarod basado en el desarrollo de la raga y heredado de Ali Akbar Khan. El valor está en el dúo en vivo: dos sistemas de resonancia e improvisación negociando la melodía en tiempo real, no una pareja genérica de world music.
es.trip_verdict: Le haría espacio activamente a este viernes local si importan las cuerdas pulsadas, la raga o la traducción musical. El encuentro supera el interés del programa solista cercano de Gripper, pero no hay estreno ni última oportunidad que justifique un rango de escasez.

events.subtitle: Jody Stephens with Mike Mills, Jon Auer, Chris Stamey and Pat Sansone
events.factual_description: Wolf Trap presents The Big Star Quintet at The Barns on Thursday, March 11, 2027 at 8:00 PM, with doors at 6:30 PM. The official bill joins Big Star drummer Jody Stephens, the last surviving member of the band's original lineup, with Mike Mills of R.E.M., Jon Auer of The Posies, Chris Stamey of The dB's and Pat Sansone of Wilco to perform Big Star's songs. The main floor is general-admission standing room and the balcony is reserved seating. Wolf Trap's presale notice places the performance in the November 10 announcement tranche, with public sales scheduled for November 13 at 10:00 AM ET.

en.why_it_matters: The specific lineup makes this more than a catalog tribute. Jody Stephens anchors the songs from inside Big Star's original history, while Mills, Auer, Stamey and Sansone come from bands that absorbed and extended its power-pop grammar. Hearing that lineage pass between its source and four descendants is the concert's real argument.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for the local March 11 date if Big Star, R.E.M. or the power-pop family tree matters. The lineup is unusually coherent and the room is intimate, but the presenter makes no farewell or one-night-only historical claim, so A+ is enough.

es.why_it_matters: La formación concreta vuelve esto más que un homenaje de catálogo. Jody Stephens sostiene las canciones desde la historia original de Big Star, mientras Mills, Auer, Stamey y Sansone vienen de bandas que absorbieron y extendieron su gramática de power pop. Escuchar cómo ese linaje pasa de la fuente a cuatro descendientes es el verdadero argumento del concierto.
es.trip_verdict: Le haría espacio activamente a la fecha local del 11 de marzo si importan Big Star, R.E.M. o el árbol genealógico del power pop. La formación es excepcionalmente coherente y la sala íntima, pero el presentador no anuncia despedida ni acontecimiento histórico de una sola noche; A+ basta.
